thread:
ana: Rain + hardwood = instant echo nightmare. Recording a 20min interview in 30min, closet booth suggestions? Pics if I try something 

ana: https://i.imgur.com/closet-mic.jpg (don't judge the laundry) :sweat_smile: 

matt: Closet's a classic. Hang a thick blanket behind you, put a small rug under your chair, close the door. Move mic 6-12 inches from mouth. Works for quick fixes. :thumbsup: 

devon: Duvet tent is my go-to for impromptu recordings. Shower rod + clamp + binder clips. Instant deadening. Also works for zooms. :tada: 

samantha: If wifi's flaky during calls, try powerline adapters or run an ethernet drop to the router. For sound, stuff some pillows behind mic stand. 

leo: For networking emergency, pocket LTE hotspot or phone tethering saved me once. Turn laptop wifi off and tether to phone; often lower latency than congested home wifi. 

hannah: Quick audio eq tip if you can post-process: high-pass at ~120Hz to kill rumble, slight dip at 200-400Hz to reduce boxiness, +3dB around 3k for presence. Command if you're using sox: `sox in.wav out.wav highpass 120 equalizer 300 1.0q -2.5 equalizer 3000 1.0q 3` 

ana: Trying closet now. If it works I'll post before/after. Also wrote to neighbor for temporary ethernet access (they said yes ???) @matt thanks for the rug idea

matt: Also, if you have pets/kids, hang a small sign on door: `Recording — please knock once` saved my sanity. :laughing:
